newsitem.title: USA: First Bank, U.S. Bancorp to merge.
newsitem.headline: First Bank, U.S. Bancorp to merge.

text.p: First Bank System Inc and U.S. Bancorp said Thursday they had signed a definitive agreement for First Bank to acquire U.S. Bancorp in a deal worth about $9 billion.
Under the agreement, U.S. Bancorp shareholders will receive, in a tax-free exchange, 0.755 share of First Bank common for each U.S. Bancorp common share.
Based on First Bank's closing stock price on March 19, this exchange ratio represents a price of $59.08 per U.S. Bancorp share, the banks said.
First Bank closed at 78-1/4 Wednesday. U.S. Bancorp closed at 48-1/4.
First Bank said it would take pre-tax merger-related charges of $625 million through the second quarter of 1998.
It said the deal is expected to be accretive to its earnings per share starting in the second quarter of 1998, nine months after closing.
By 1999, First Bank sees earnings per share accretion of about eight percent.
First Bank Chairman, Chief Executive and President John Grundhofer will be president and chief executive of the merged bank, which will be called U.S. Bancorp, the banks said.
U.S. Bancorp Chairman and Chief Executive Gerry Cameron will serve as chairman of the merged bank until his retirement in 1998.
First Bank said it sees pre-tax cost savings of about $340 million from the merger. The banks see their combined operating expenses being reduced by 14 percent.
About 4,000 jobs will be eliminated as a result of the merger, the banks said.
First Bank said its board had rescinded its stock repurchase authorization.
Pursuant to the merger agreement, the two banks said each has granted the other an option to acquire 19.9 percent of its stock.
The acquisition, to be accounted for as a pooling of interests, is expected to close in the third quarter of 1997, the banks said.
